source: the atoms walkthrough (gate-critical per specs/07 P0): importance is structural never volumetric; record vs extract; the split judgment

fixtures.title: Three texts, huge importance (Thiel day)
fixtures.raw: [3 messages] 'Sam — Nina from the Thiel Fellowship team. Peter's office flagged your agents work.' 'We'd love a 15-min intro call Friday 10am PT — does that work?' 'If yes I'll send a calendar invite from this number's email.'

args.summary: Nina from the Thiel Fellowship reached out — Peter's office flagged the agents work; proposed a 15-min intro call Friday 10am PT.
quotes: Peter's office flagged your agents work

args.description: Reply to Nina (Thiel Fellowship) — confirm Friday 10am PT intro call
Nina to send the calendar invite after confirmation

must_not: under-extraction because the volume is tiny — 3 texts can outrank a hundred
notable asserted at filing (it is assigned at the daily pass; meta.notable_candidate is the correct filer-level signal)
tolerances: reply-task due same-day, time free (high urgency is the point)
expectation optional until Sam confirms — but the labeled default keeps it (reliability on follow-through)
fixtures.walkthrough_law: importance is structural, never volumetric — this day's 3 texts outrank t02's 75

fixtures.title: 75 texts, one honest line (meme day)
fixtures.raw: [thread-day window: 75 messages in the Layton sibs group — memes, reaction gifs, laughing at a video Josh sent. No questions, no commitments, no new handles, no plans.]

args.summary: Active day in the Layton sibs thread (75 messages) — memes and banter, no commitments or questions.

must_not: an LLM pass at all — zero detected signal means the deterministic template emits the atom
discard (this is the relationship record: not-recording is irreversible)
tolerances: summary is the template's output — wording fixed by template, message count and participants interpolated
fixtures.walkthrough_law: record everything non-spam; extract conservatively — one honest line feeds the family-coverage record

fixtures.title: One thread-day, two glaringly distinct purposes (the split judgment)
fixtures.raw: [thread-day window, same Layton sibs group] MORNING (9:02-9:40): planning Dad's 60th — Emma: 'June 28 dinner, that steakhouse he loves?' Josh: 'in.' Sam: 'I'll book it for 7pm, 6 people.' EVENING (20:15-21:30): Emma: 'Mom's MRI results came back, can we talk?' — long careful conversation about results, next steps, who calls the doctor Friday.

args.summary: Planned Dad's 60th with Josh and Emma — June 28 steakhouse dinner; Sam booking for 7pm, 6 people.

args.description: Book steakhouse for Dad's 60th — June 28, 7pm, 6 people

args.summary: Long talk with Emma and Josh about Mom's MRI results and next steps; someone calls the doctor Friday.

must_not: one merged atom burying the MRI conversation inside birthday logistics — the purposes are glaringly distinct
more than two atoms (no micro-chunking the planning back-and-forth)
a fabricated 'call the doctor' task for Sam (who calls was not settled — it lives in the atom; the daily pass may surface it as a question)
tolerances: booking-task due date free (before June 28, reasonably soon)
sensitivity 1 on the MRI atom is the labeled default — Sam confirms where health content sits
summaries free; both must name participants and the load-bearing facts
fixtures.walkthrough_law: default 1 atom per thread-day; split ONLY when purposes are glaringly distinct — this is the canonical split case
